post.description: Sends for both existing and unknown addresses without revealing account existence. Does not create an account. Mailbox budget shared across API instances: one send per minute, five per hour, plus existing IP auth limiter. SMTP failure invalidates the code and returns 503. No development code is exposed or logged.

post.summary: Sign in or create an account with an email code
post.description: Codes expire after ten minutes, allow five guesses, and are consumed atomically once. A resend replaces the previous challenge. Verification preserves existing roles, permissions and Google IDs; a new account needs all four profile fields and obeys the signup pause. A successful code check consumes the code even if later profile or signup checks reject the request; request a new code after correcting the problem. Invitation codes cannot be used here.

post.summary: Email a code to the invited address
post.description: Derives recipient from the invitation; ignores any supplied email. Only pending or already accepted invitations qualify. Binds the challenge to this exact invitation link. Uses the same mailbox resend and hourly budget as Personal sign-in.

post.summary: Accept an invitation using Google or an emailed code
post.description: A pending, unexpired emailed invitation token verifies exactly its stored email once. No Google credential or additional emailed code is needed for initial acceptance. Replays without independent authentication return 401, including concurrent submissions. Accepted links require Google or an invitation-bound email code. Acceptance rechecks revocation, expiry, inviter permissions, enrollment, seats, entitlements and membership under the existing row lock. Platform invitations retain the signup-pause exception; organization invitations do not bypass it.

credential.description: Optional Google credential. Accepted invitations require this or challengeId and code; pending invitations can be accepted using the token alone.

configuration: Existing SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS and SMTP_FROM are reused; SMTP TLS remains required.
Set EMAIL_CODE_SECRET (recommended) or reuse the mandatory production JWT_SECRET. Keep it stable across API instances. Rotating it invalidates outstanding codes.
Apply migration before releasing the API. Generate the Prisma client. Grant the restricted runtime role SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on EmailSignInCode.
Release API before web. Google remains available throughout rollout.
Remove abandoned EmailSignInCode rows whose sentAt is older than one day during normal database maintenance. Preserve recent rows to retain mailbox budgets.
